tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P1] Derive shape, fill and badge from `kind` on IdentityAvatar and narrow AgentAvatar
tasks.description:
Make the square/fill/Bot convention structural instead of opt-in, at the two files that carry every other surface (spec §W1.1, §W1.2).

1. `apps/client/src/layers/shared/ui/identity-avatar.tsx` gains two props: `kind?: AuthorKind` ('human' | 'agent' | 'system', the type imported from `@dorkos/shared/room-schemas` — do NOT invent a 'person' spelling, §W1.1 says why) and `origin?: IdentityOrigin` (already defined at `shared/ui/identity-origin.ts`, read only to derive an external badge). Derivation table, exactly: agent -> shape 'square', variant 'fill', badge `<Bot />`; human with local/absent origin -> circle, tint, no badge; human with `origin: { platform }` -> circle, tint, `ADAPTER_LOGO_MAP[platform] ?? <Send />` (`ADAPTER_LOGO_MAP` from `@dorkos/icons`); system -> circle, tint, no badge; `kind` omitted -> circle, tint, no badge (byte-identical to today, so this is additive and no existing call site changes meaning).
2. Explicit props win per axis: passing `shape`, `variant` or `badge` steps the derivation aside for that axis only. Change the badge render guard at `identity-avatar.tsx:183` from `badge !== undefined` to `badge != null`, so `badge={null}` is a real opt-out and renders no empty plate.
3. `IdentityAvatar` gains `working?: boolean` — a top-right pulsing dot mirroring the bottom-right badge slot. Use the `bg-status-success` token (never `bg-emerald-500`, which `.claude/rules/components.md` bans), ring it in `bg-background`, and drop the ping under `motion-reduce:hidden` while keeping the dot. It is deliberately kind-agnostic.
4. `apps/client/src/layers/entities/agent/ui/AgentAvatar.tsx` stops extending `VariantProps<typeof identityAvatarVariants>` (`:21`) — that extension is exactly how a caller could pass `shape="circle"` and re-break the convention. Its props become `{ color, emoji, size?, healthStatus?, working?, imageUrl?, className? }` and it hard-passes `kind="agent"`. Delete its hand-rolled dot (`:49-53`) in favour of the new `working` prop. The health ring stays exactly where it is (`HEALTH_RING[healthStatus]` merged through `className`, `:47`) — mesh vocabulary must not move into `shared/`.
5. Do NOT edit the twelve `AgentAvatar` call sites. Verified by grep: every production call site passes only `color`, `emoji`, `size`, `healthStatus`, `className`, so narrowing is source-compatible and all twelve inherit square/fill/Bot from this one edit (spec §W1.2 lists them).
6. Add the kind matrix to the playground: extend the existing `IdentityAvatar` showcase (`apps/client/src/dev/showcases/IdentityShowcases.tsx`, registered at `dev/sections/components-sections.ts:248-267`) with agent / human-local / human-external / system states. Keep its id, title and `/dev/components#identityavatar` anchor unchanged.
7. Document the convention once, in `contributing/design-system.md`: a short Identity section carrying the kind -> shape/variant/badge table and pointing at `identity-avatar.tsx` as the implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- jsdom test: `<IdentityAvatar kind="agent" />` asserts the square radius class, the solid `backgroundColor` and a `Bot` badge; `human` local asserts circle/tint/no badge; `human` external asserts the platform glyph; `system` asserts circle/tint/no badge.
- jsdom test: `<IdentityAvatar kind="agent" shape="circle" />` is round, and `badge={null}` renders no plate.
- jsdom test: the `working` dot renders, uses `status-success`, and the ping is hidden under `motion-reduce`.
- A `@ts-expect-error` line in the `AgentAvatar` test asserts `shape` is no longer assignable — a compile-time check that cannot silently pass.
- `apps/client/src/layers/entities/agent/__tests__/agent-identity.test.tsx:18-57` currently asserts `rounded-full` and the emerald dot. Those assertions are the red-before/green-after evidence for this change: UPDATE them to assert the square radius, the fill background and the `status-success` dot. Do not delete them.
- `grep -rn "bg-emerald-500\|animate-ping" apps/client/src/layers` returns hits only in `identity-avatar.tsx` (`RoomMemberRow`'s copy is removed in task 1.2).
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client lint` pass.
tasks.acceptance: IdentityAvatar derives shape/variant/badge from `kind` with per-axis explicit overrides; `badge={null}` opts out; `working` dot lives in one place; AgentAvatar's props no longer admit shape/variant and hard-pass kind='agent'; twelve call sites unchanged and all render square/fill/Bot; playground matrix and design-system doc updated; tests above green.

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P1] Resolve every identity face through one shared function and fix the room surfaces
tasks.description:
Absorbs DOR-962 ("one agent, one face"). `RoomMemberRow` and `MemberList` each hand-roll the same face-resolution ladder one file apart and disagree about the shape/badge decision — the sharpest violation in the audit (spec §W1.4).

1. Add `apps/client/src/layers/shared/lib/identity-face.ts` exporting `IdentityFace { kind: AuthorKind; color: string; emoji?: string; imageUrl?: string; fallback: string; origin?: IdentityOrigin }` and a pure `resolveIdentityFace(input: IdentityFaceInput): IdentityFace`. Precedence, highest first: an explicit `override` (an agent's own manifest colour/icon, which only a feature-layer caller can reach), then the author record's render cache, then a colour hashed from the opaque id plus the first letter of the display name. It takes NO agent types — that is the point: `MemberList` lives in `entities/room` and may not import `entities/agent`, which is exactly why the two implementations diverged. Barrel-export it from `shared/lib/index.ts`.
2. `apps/client/src/layers/features/room-management/ui/RoomMemberRow.tsx:185-213` — delete the inline ladder, the `badge={isAgent ? <Bot /> : undefined}` decision and the hand-rolled working dot (`:196-213`). It passes the `resolveAgentVisual()` override it already computes into `resolveIdentityFace`, then renders one `IdentityAvatar` with `kind`, `working` and the resolved face.
3. `apps/client/src/layers/entities/room/ui/MemberList.tsx:86-100` — same replacement, with no override. The badge asymmetry (Bot in one file, external-only in the other) disappears because neither file decides it any more.
4. `apps/client/src/layers/entities/room/ui/RoomAvatar.tsx:97` — a DM counterpart is always an agent (`room-display.ts:104-108`), so pass `kind="agent"` on both the single and the stacked faces. This also fixes the sidebar room row (`RoomRow.tsx:330,367`), the room header masthead (`RoomHeader.tsx:48`) and the command-palette room row (`RoomCommandItem.tsx:48`), which all render through it.
5. Playground: add a `RoomAvatar` showcase (channel `#` glyph, single DM face, stacked faces, letter fallback — now kind-aware) to `apps/client/src/dev/showcases/RoomsShowcases.tsx` with its registry entry in `dev/sections/rooms-sections.ts`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit table over `resolveIdentityFace` covering override-wins, cache-wins, hash-fallback, and the empty-display-name edge.
- jsdom test asserting `RoomMemberRow` and `MemberList` render THE SAME shape and badge for the same member — the regression that made this the sharpest violation. It must fail against today's code.
- jsdom test: an agent DM face from `RoomAvatar` is square/filled.
- `grep -rn "bg-emerald-500\|animate-ping" apps/client/src/layers` now returns only `identity-avatar.tsx`.
- `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/dev/__tests__/playground-registry.test.ts` green (the new showcase needs its registry entry and a literal title).
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck` and `lint` pass.
tasks.acceptance: One pure `resolveIdentityFace` in shared/lib; RoomMemberRow, MemberList and RoomAvatar all render through it; an agent and a human in the same room list have visibly different silhouettes; parity test green.
tasks.activeForm: Unifying identity face resolution across the room surfaces

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P1] Collapse the duplicate agent rows and pickers and end the OriginMark name collision
tasks.description:
Three independent dedupes from spec §W1.5. Each has a named boundary — do not extend any of them past it.

1. Single-select agent row. `features/tasks/ui/AgentPicker.tsx:53` and `features/command-palette/ui/AgentCommandItem.tsx:71` are both `Command`-based rows drawing avatar + name + secondary text off `resolveAgentVisual`. Extract `entities/agent/ui/AgentOptionRow.tsx` with props `{ agent, secondary?, trailing?, selected? }` and consume it from both (both are features, both may import entities). `AgentChipPicker` STAYS SEPARATE — its multi-select keyboard model is genuinely different and merging it would be coincidental-duplication extraction under `.claude/rules/conventions.md`.
2. `COLOR_PRESETS` is duplicated byte-identically at `features/agent-settings/ui/IdentityTab.tsx:36-47` and `features/agent-hub/ui/AvatarPickerPopover.tsx:12-23`. Move it to `shared/lib/favicon-utils.ts` beside `EMOJI_SET` (which is ALREADY shared and barrel-exported at `shared/lib/index.ts:93` — the audit was wrong about it) and barrel-export it. Then collapse the two swatch/emoji GRIDS into one `entities/agent/ui/AvatarPickerGrid.tsx`. The two CONTAINERS stay: an inline full-width panel with the celebration animation, and two `ResponsivePopover`s, are genuinely different surfaces.
3. Name collision. `entities/session/ui/OriginMark.tsx:34` (where a session was started) and `entities/room/ui/OriginMark.tsx:46` (a security-relevant "not from this machine" mark) share a name and are one autocomplete away from an import bug. Rename the SESSION one to `SessionOriginMark`; the room one keeps its name because it matches the domain word used in `AuthorOrigin` and `identity-origin.ts`. Full rename set: `entities/session/ui/OriginMark.tsx` -> `SessionOriginMark.tsx` with the export renamed; `entities/session/ui/__tests__/OriginMark.test.tsx` -> `SessionOriginMark.test.tsx` with its 5 assertions updated; `entities/session/index.ts:136` barrel export; `entities/session/ui/SessionRowCompact.tsx:13,140`; `entities/session/ui/SessionRowFull.tsx:25,257`; `features/dashboard-sidebar/ui/RecentSessionRow.tsx:8,47`; `features/top-nav/ui/SessionHeader.tsx:4,47`; `features/dashboard-sidebar/__tests__/DashboardSidebar.test.tsx:284` mock key.
4. Provenance-chip consolidation is explicitly NOT done here. `OriginMark` x2, `AccountMark` and `RuntimeMark` share an interaction shape and nothing else; a generic `Mark` base would be an abstraction over a coincidence (§W1.5 #7, recorded as considered and declined).
5. Playground: add an `AvatarPickerGrid` showcase rendering the unified grid in both its containers, registered in `dev/sections/`.

Acceptance criteria:
- `grep -rn "COLOR_PRESETS\s*=" apps/client/src` returns exactly one definition.
- `grep -rn "export function OriginMark" apps/client/src` returns exactly one.
- jsdom test for `AgentOptionRow` covering selected, secondary and trailing states; the existing `AgentPicker` and `AgentCommandItem` tests still pass unchanged in behaviour.
- The renamed `SessionOriginMark.test.tsx` passes with its 5 updated assertions.
- `pnpm knip` reports no new dead exports.
- `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/dev/__tests__/playground-registry.test.ts` green.
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck` and `lint` pass.

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P2] Serve one roster of every identity on this install from GET /api/team
tasks.description:
One read-only aggregation over the identity stores that already exist. It writes nothing, mints nothing and has no POST — that is ADR `260806-222535` (spec §W2.2).

1. `packages/shared/src/team-schemas.ts` (new, plus a `./team-schemas` entry in the `exports` map of `packages/shared/package.json`): `TeamSourceWarningSchema { source: string; message: string }`; `TeamRosterResponseSchema { members: TeamMember[]; warnings?: TeamSourceWarning[] }` where `warnings` is OMITTED entirely on a clean read, never `[]`; `TeamMemberSchema { id, kind (AuthorKindSchema — reused, never forked), displayName, handle: string | null, emoji?, color?, imageUrl?, isSelf: boolean, ownerId: string | null, origin (AuthorOriginSchema), agent?: TeamAgentFacts, person?: TeamPersonFacts }`. `TeamAgentFactsSchema { manifestId, runtime, model?, healthStatus, working, namespace?, projectPath?, isDefault, isSystem, registeredAt }`. `TeamPersonFactsSchema { role: string | null, email?: string }`. `ownerId` is REQUIRED and nullable from the first commit — a schema that lets it be absent is how it becomes optional in practice (§Testing Strategy).
2. `apps/server/src/services/identity/` — a new service domain justified under `.claude/rules/server-structure.md` because it will hold `aggregate-team.ts`, `operator-profile.ts`, `avatar-store.ts` and `local-avatar-store.ts`: "who is on this install, and what they look like". It belongs to neither `rooms/` nor `mesh/` because it reads both.
3. `aggregate-team.ts` sources: people from `authors` where `retired_at IS NULL` and `kind = 'human'` — `AuthorRegistry` has no list method today (`getById:614` and `getMany:626` are the only reads), so add `listActive(kind?: AuthorKind): AuthorRecord[]` following the existing `activeRow` query shape (`:348`); agents from `meshCore.listWithHealth(...)`, the same read `GET /api/mesh/agents` (`routes/mesh.ts:376-385`) already uses — add no new mesh query.
4. `operator-profile.ts` resolves the operator's display name by an explicit precedence that NEVER depends on `authors.display_name` first: `findOwnerAccount()?.name` (`services/core/auth/accounts.ts:45-54`) -> `config.profile.displayName` (`UserProfileSchema`) -> the author record's `displayName` -> `'You'`. Do NOT change `LOCAL_HUMAN_DISPLAY_NAME = 'You'` (`author-registry.ts:74`) and do NOT touch `bindOwner` (`:553`). The two contexts diverge on purpose: a room renders `'You'` from the operator's own seat; a roster has no "you" framing and renders the real name.
5. `ownerId`: every non-system agent read from the local mesh gets the operator's roster id. A system agent (`isSystem`, i.e. DorkBot) gets `null` — it belongs to the install, not to a person. Semantically this is `CommunityMemberSchema.ownerMemberId` (`community-adapter.ts:456-464`) spelled in this payload's ids.
6. `person.email` is returned ONLY on the viewer's own row, enforced in the aggregation, even on a single-user install.
7. Degradation in the ADR-0310 shape: each source read in its own try/catch with the same 2s timeout constant `aggregate-session-list.ts:25` uses; a failure pushes `{ source, message }` and the other sources still return. A total failure of one source is a degraded roster, never a 500.
8. `apps/server/src/routes/team.ts`, mounted in `apps/server/src/index.ts` beside the other injected-singleton routers (it needs `meshCore`, the `AuthorRegistry` and the db). Add a `registry.registerPath` entry in `services/core/openapi-registry.ts` whose description cites the degradation contract, matching the `/api/sessions` entry at `:362-384`.

Acceptance criteria:
- `packages/shared` unit tests: the response schema parses a full row and a minimal row, refuses a row missing `ownerId`, and accepts an absent `warnings` key.
- Server test: the roster contains exactly one `kind: 'human'` row with `isSelf: true`, one row per registered agent, `ownerId` equal to the operator's id on every non-system agent and `null` on DorkBot, and `warnings` ABSENT on a clean read.
- Server test: stub the mesh read to throw; the people rows still return with `warnings: [{ source: 'agents', ... }]` and HTTP 200.
- Server test: with an owner account named `Dorian`, the roster returns `Dorian`, not `You`; and a room roster read in the same test still renders `You`. Both halves, or the divergence is not pinned. This test fails against today's code.
- Server test: `person.email` is present on the self row and absent on every other row.
- `/api/docs` lists `GET /api/team`.
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/shared build`, `pnpm --filter @dorkos/server typecheck`, `lint` and the server suite pass.
tasks.acceptance: GET /api/team returns one roster over `authors` + `agents` with per-source warnings, the operator's real name, ownerId on every non-system agent, and email only on the self row; no write path exists.
tasks.activeForm: Building the team roster aggregation endpoint

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P2] Show every person and agent on this install as one card roster at /team
tasks.description:
The roster surface itself — cards, filters, grouping and search (spec §W2.3, §W2.4, §W2.6). Depends on DOR-676 for real handles; ships with `handle: null` rendered honestly (no bare `@`) if DOR-676 has not landed.

1. `apps/client/src/layers/entities/team/` — a new entity slice: `api/` (the transport call), `model/use-team-roster.ts` (TanStack Query keyed `['team']`), and the derived selectors the page needs. `entities/` is correct: the roster is a domain object several features and one widget read, and it must not live in the widget that happens to render it first.
2. `apps/client/src/layers/widgets/team/ui/TeamPage.tsx` — a widget because it composes several features. Cards, chips, the group toggle and the view switch are feature-layer components under `features/team-roster/`; the identity primitives they use stay in `shared/` and `entities/`.
3. Cards view (the default): ONE unified grid, operator first, then agents — chosen over a sectioned roster because the shape/badge language does the distinguishing and sections would say the same thing twice. Each card carries the identity disc at `md`, the display name, the `@handle`, a kind-specific second line (agent: `runtime · model`; person: `role` or `On this machine`), a working dot when live, and on an agent a `by @handle` owner attribution rendered as a BUTTON that filters the roster to that owner.
4. Filter chips `All · People · Agents`, then one chip per person once more than one exists. Chips write `?kind=` / `?owner=` so a filtered roster is a shareable URL. `?group=manager` re-clusters agent cards under a header row per owner (the person's own compact lockup), unowned identities last. `?q=` matches display name and handle case-insensitively over the already-loaded roster — no server round trip; the roster is bounded by the agents on one machine.
5. Empty and degraded states: reuse `features/agents-list`'s `AgentGhostRows` for the no-agents state, now with the operator's own card above it — the roster is never empty, because the person reading it is on it. When `warnings` is present, show a dismissible inline banner naming the source that failed ("Couldn't read your agents — showing who we could."), written to the `writing-for-humans` bar.
6. Mobile: one column below `md` (768px, `use-is-mobile.ts:3`); the chip row scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping to three lines.
7. Two binding rules for the Buzz future (§W2.6), both testable today: NO component may branch on "there is exactly one person" — rendering, grouping and filtering read the roster as a list; and NO component may assume `isSelf` for a person — `isSelf` is a flag on one row and "you" is a CHIP, not a code path.
8. Playground: a `Team Card` section rendering operator, agent-with-owner, external person, and long name/handle states.

Acceptance criteria:
- jsdom tests over `TeamPage`: filter chips, the owner filter, manager grouping, search, the empty state and the warnings banner.
- The grouping and grid tests run against a fixture with TWO people, four agents and two owners — a shape the product cannot produce yet, which is precisely why the test exists. It must fail against any component that assumes one person.
- jsdom test: a member with `handle: null` renders no `@` at all, rather than one that reaches nobody.
- `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/dev/__tests__/playground-registry.test.ts` green.
- FSD layer lint clean (`shared <- entities <- features <- widgets`); imports go through barrel `index.ts` files only.
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck`, `lint` and the client suite pass.
tasks.acceptance: A card roster renders the operator first and every agent under them, with kind chips, an owner filter, a manager grouping, search, a degraded banner and a one-column mobile layout — all driven by URL params and all correct against a two-person fixture.
tasks.activeForm: Building the Team roster cards, filters and grouping

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P2] Replace /agents with /team everywhere and delete the old fleet page
tasks.description:
The route swap, the table and topology views, and the removal of the page they came from (spec §W2.1, §W2.5).

1. `apps/client/src/router.tsx`: a `/team` route with `validateSearch: zodValidator(teamSearchSchema)` -> `TeamPage`. `teamSearchSchema = mergeDialogSearch(...)` over: `view: 'cards' | 'table' | 'topology' | 'denied' | 'access'` default `'cards'`, where `'list'` is ACCEPTED and normalized to `'table'` via a `z.preprocess` because `/agents?view=list` is a live external address used by the media-capture pipeline (`apps/e2e/capture/surfaces-desktop.ts:48,498`); `kind: 'all' | 'people' | 'agents'` default `'all'`; `owner: string`; `group: 'none' | 'manager'` default `'none'`; `q: string`; `member: string`; `agent: string` (retained, the topology detail-panel selection); `sort` retained from `agentsSearchSchema:128`; `agentFilterSchema.searchValidator` retained.
2. `/agents` survives as a redirect and NOTHING else: a route with the same `validateSearch` whose `beforeLoad` throws `redirect({ to: '/team', search, replace: true })`. AGENTS.md says a superseded thing is removed, so state the justification in the PR: every in-repo caller is swept in the same change, and what the alias serves is addresses this repo does not control — a bookmark, a docs link, and the Electron shell's persisted tab list, which stores raw pathnames (`app/__tests__/use-electron-close-tab.test.tsx:57-126`). A persisted tab pointing at a dead route is a blank window on next launch.
3. Sweep the 13 in-repo call sites: `features/mesh/ui/ImportProjectsDialog.tsx:59`; `features/settings/ui/external-mcp/ExternalMcpCard.tsx:201`; `features/feature-promos/ui/dialogs/AgentChatDialog.tsx:12`; `features/dashboard-sidebar/ui/SidebarNavHeader.tsx:53-54`; `features/command-palette/model/use-palette-actions.ts:124,199`; `features/top-nav/ui/AgentsHeader.tsx:35`; `features/dashboard-status/ui/SystemStatusRow.tsx:91`; `widgets/agents/ui/AgentsPage.tsx:123,136,150,161,183`; `AppShell.tsx:190` (`case '/agents'` -> `case '/team'`); `apps/e2e/capture/surfaces-desktop.ts:48,55,379,498,713`; `apps/e2e/tests/agents/agents-page.spec.ts` plus its `apps/e2e/manifest.json:341` entry.
4. Nav: `SidebarNavHeader.tsx:50-56` — label `Agents` -> `Team`, icon `Users` unchanged (and now literally right), `isActive` on `/team`, `to: '/team'`. `TOUR_ANCHORS.navAgents` KEEPS its key — renaming a tour anchor breaks the persisted tour position for no user gain — and gains a comment saying why.
5. Table view seeded from `features/agents-list/lib/agent-columns.tsx`. Its `IdentityCell` (`:73-108`) inherits kind-awareness through `AgentAvatar`; the table gains a `Managed by` column; people rows render the columns that apply and blanks where they do not (a person has no runtime). The view switch DROPS the table option below `md` — a 6-column table on a phone is not a view — leaving cards and topology.

tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P3] Store profile photos locally behind a seam a cloud backend can implement later
tasks.description:
The seam is the requirement (ideation D5, Dorian explicit). The route depends on an interface, never on the disk (spec §W3.5).

1. `apps/server/src/services/identity/avatar-store.ts` — `interface AvatarStore { put(id, bytes: Buffer, contentType: AvatarContentType): Promise<{ url: string }>; get(id): Promise<{ stream: Readable; contentType: string; etag: string } | null>; delete(id): Promise<void> }`. `put` returns the URL a render cache stores, and that IS the whole seam: today `LocalAvatarStore` returns a server-relative `/api/profile/avatar/<id>?v=<hash>`; a future server- or cloud-backed store returns an absolute `https://...` and not one renderer, schema or component changes. Nothing above this interface may construct a path, join a directory, or assume the bytes are local.
2. `local-avatar-store.ts` is the only implementation today. It writes `<dorkHome>/avatars/<authorId>.<ext>` where `dorkHome` comes from `resolveDorkHome()` (`apps/server/src/lib/dork-home.ts:15-21`). NEVER `os.homedir()` — banned in `apps/server/src` outside three carve-outs (Hard Rule 3, `.claude/rules/dork-home.md`). This is deliberately NOT the existing upload directory: `UploadHandler.getUploadDir(cwd)` (`services/core/upload-handler.ts:28`) is `{cwd}/.dork/.temp/uploads`, per-project and temporary; an avatar is per-install and permanent.
3. `POST /api/profile/avatar` in `apps/server/src/routes/profile.ts` — multipart via a DEDICATED multer instance (the one in `routes/uploads.ts:19-67` is cwd-scoped and config-driven and is not reusable here). Rules: <= 2 MB enforced by multer `limits` BEFORE a byte is written (a cap enforced post-write is a disk-fill bug); png/jpeg/webp only, validated by MAGIC BYTES, not by the extension or the `Content-Type` the client claims; SVG refused outright — it is a script vector and `files.ts:109-116` needs a bespoke CSP header to serve one safely, which a profile photo has no reason to need; no re-encoding and no resizing, because that needs `sharp` and this spec adds no dependency. Writes go through the store, then update `authors.image_url` AND Better Auth `user.image` with the same URL, so the account record and the roster cannot disagree.
4. `DELETE /api/profile/avatar` clears all three.
5. `GET /api/profile/avatar/:id` modelled on `routes/files.ts:49-135`: `createReadStream(...).pipe(res)`, `Content-Type` from the stored type, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a strong `ETag` from the content hash, and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. The `?v=<hash>` in `imageUrl` is what makes a replaced photo appear immediately without disabling caching.
6. `registry.registerPath` entries so both routes appear at `/api/docs`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Roundtrip server test: POST a 1x1 PNG; a file lands under `<dorkHome>/avatars/`; the response `url` round-trips through GET with the right `Content-Type` and `nosniff`; `authors.image_url` and `user.image` both hold it; DELETE clears all three.
- Negative cases that MUST fail the request: a 3 MB file (413/400), an SVG, and a `.png` whose magic bytes say GIF.
- Path containment: an `authorId` containing `..` or `/` cannot escape `<dorkHome>/avatars/` — the same containment check `routes/uploads.ts:84-91` makes. Overwrite replaces; delete is idempotent.
- Seam test: substitute a fake `AvatarStore` returning `https://cdn.example/x.png` and assert the roster's `imageUrl` is that absolute URL with NO route, schema or client change. This is the assertion that makes the sync-ready claim true rather than asserted.
- `scripts/test-homedir-guard.sh` passes with the new files.
- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/server typecheck`, `lint` and the server suite pass.
tasks.acceptance: An AvatarStore interface with a local implementation under <dorkHome>/avatars/; POST/GET/DELETE /api/profile/avatar with magic-byte validation, a 2 MB pre-write cap, no SVG, nosniff and content-hash ETags; the substitution test proves the seam.

The two surfaces where the person at the keyboard is finally a person (spec §W3.1, §W3.3, §W3.6). The handle field needs DOR-676; everything else ships without it.

ACCOUNT MENU. There is no user or account element anywhere in the shell today (verified by grep). It is icon-sized — the operator's `IdentityAvatar` at `size="sm"` — so it sits in a row of peers without re-laying-out the footer, and it does not displace the brand link, which is a different affordance. Build it as a `ResponsiveDropdownMenu` (`shared/ui/responsive-dropdown-menu.tsx:34`), which gives the mobile behaviour for free. KNOWN VERIFICATION POINT: on mobile the sidebar is itself a `Sheet` (`shared/ui/sidebar.tsx:179-201`), so this opens a vaul `Drawer` inside a Radix `Dialog` — a composition used nowhere else in the app today. Check it in a real browser at 375px. If it misbehaves, the fallback is `ResponsiveDropdownMenu` forced to its dropdown branch inside the sheet.

SETTINGS › PROFILE. `SETTINGS_TABS` (`features/settings/ui/SettingsDialog.tsx:27-74`) gains `{ id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', icon: UserRound, component: ProfileTab }` as the FIRST entry. Promotion needs nothing else: ungrouped tabs render above the first group header (`shared/ui/tabbed-dialog.tsx:123-131`). `SettingsTab` (`shared/model/app-store/app-store-panels.ts:16-26`) gains `'profile'`, so `?settings=profile` works through the existing deep-link machinery — which is exactly what the drawer's Edit button calls. tasks.subject: [identity-consistency] [P4] Give identity one Dev Playground page with the gaps closed and the mocks unified
tasks.description:
The last phase on purpose: a playground page that showcases half a convention is a page that has to be rebuilt (spec §W4).

REGISTRATION — SEVEN touch points, not six. The audit lists six; missing the seventh turns the drift test red in CI. (1) `dev/playground-registry.ts:2-22` — `'identity'` in the `Page` union. (2) `dev/sections/identity-sections.ts` — NEW, exporting `IDENTITY_SECTIONS`. (3) `dev/playground-registry.ts:38-56` (named re-export) AND `:59-104` (aliased import + spread into `PLAYGROUND_REGISTRY`). (4) `dev/playground-config.ts` — import plus a `PageConfig` entry (`id: 'identity'`, `group: 'agents'`, `path: 'identity'`, icon, description). (5) `dev/pages/IdentityPage.tsx` — NEW, via `PlaygroundPageLayout`. (6) `dev/DevPlayground.tsx:88-109` — `PAGE_COMPONENTS` entry plus import. (7) `dev/__tests__/playground-registry.test.ts:5-26` and `:51-71` — the union assertion hardcodes all 19 section arrays by name; without `IDENTITY_SECTIONS` there, "PLAYGROUND_REGISTRY equals the union of all page-level arrays" fails. Placement is the AGENTS group (ideation D6), beside Subsystems and Rooms.

CROSS-LISTING IS BY RENDERING, NOT BY DOUBLE-REGISTRATION. The registry enforces `id === slugify(title)` and no duplicate ids across the whole registry, so one title holds exactly one entry, pinned to one page and one `/dev/<page>#<anchor>` URL. Therefore: the three `shared/ui` primitives — `IdentityAvatar` (`components-sections.ts:248-267`), `MentionPill` (`:268-287`), `IdentityHoverCard` (`:288-304`) — KEEP `page: 'components'`, their ids, their titles and their existing `/dev/components#...` anchors. `IdentityPage.tsx` imports and RENDERS those same showcase components; the drift check scans FILES (`readRenderedSections()`, `:154-167`, walking `dev/showcases/*.tsx` and `dev/pages/*.tsx`), so a second page rendering an already-registered showcase adds no new rendered title and both drift directions stay green. The Identity page's TOC is still complete because `PageConfig.sections` is COMPOSED: `[...IDENTITY_SECTIONS, ...COMPONENTS_SECTIONS.filter((s) => IDENTITY_PRIMITIVE_IDS.has(s.id))]` — legal because `PLAYGROUND_REGISTRY` is the union of the per-page `*_SECTIONS` arrays, not of `PAGE_CONFIGS[].sections`, and the containment assertion holds because each borrowed entry is in the registry exactly once. The accepted cost, stated rather than discovered: those three sections still group under "Components" in Cmd+K and their canonical URL stays `/dev/components#identityavatar`. That is the trade for not breaking a single existing anchor.

SECTIONS THAT GENUINELY MOVE (their entry moves array and its `page` changes, so their anchor changes): `AgentAvatar` and `AgentIdentity`, `features-sections.ts:26-40` -> Identity. They are entity-layer identity components, "Subsystems" is not where anyone looks for them, and nothing outside this repo links to a playground anchor. `RoomMemberRow` (`rooms-sections.ts:33-37`), `MessageAuthorAvatar` (`chat-sections.ts:40-59`) and `AgentIdentityChip` (`chat-sections.ts:567-582`) STAY registered where they are and are cross-listed by rendering — each is primarily a room or chat surface.

NEW COVERAGE on the Identity page: `RoomPresenceLine` (the room's live working line) and an `Identity Shape Matrix` (agent x human-local x human-external x system, crossed with image / emoji / letter — the whole convention on one screen). The `RoomAvatar`, `AvatarPickerGrid`, `Account Menu`, `Profile Drawer` and `Team Card` sections are built by tasks 1.2, 1.4, 3.6, 3.4 and 2.2 respectively; this task composes them onto the page, it does not rebuild them.

OUT OF SCOPE — square-at-xs/sm sizes. `Identity Sizes` (every kind at xs/sm/md/lg) is IN PROGRESS as DOR-955 in another session. Do NOT build a second sizes showcase. If DOR-955 has landed, compose its existing section into the Identity page's TOC by id; if it has not, leave the slot out and say so in the PR.

MOCK DATA. `dev/showcases/AgentIdentityShowcases.tsx:7-18` uses its own inline `SAMPLE`/`AGENTS` consts. DELETE them; every identity showcase draws from `MOCK_IDENTITIES` (`dev/mock-samples.ts:809-872`), extended with `imageUrl`, `ownerHandle` and `working` on `MockIdentity` (`:792-800`) and a cast member carrying a photo as a small inline data URI.

THE `category` CORRECTION. `category` is dead metadata: nothing reads `.category` anywhere (`PlaygroundSearch.tsx:18-25,63-79` groups by `section.page`; `TocSidebar` renders flat). KEEP it — it is in-file documentation on 241 entries and churning them buys no user anything — but stop it lying: correct its TSDoc in `playground-registry.ts` to say it is documentation-only and not a search grouping, and correct `.claude/skills/maintaining-dev-playground/SKILL.md`'s claim that it "controls search grouping in Cmd+K results", since that sentence is what would otherwise make the next author build on it.
